problem: Embodied QA methods (PACMAN, NMC) are assumed to need navigation and vision, but nobody checked how much of their accuracy is just dataset bias in EQAv1. No question-only baselines had been reported.
motivation: If a model that never sees the environment matches or beats navigation+VQA agents, the benchmark does not measure embodied reasoning and reported progress is misleading. Prior work on VQA, NLI and Story-cloze had already found that biases let degenerate baselines win.
key_idea: Question-only (blindfold) baselines, an averaged-BoW linear classifier and a nearest-neighbor answer-distribution lookup, match or beat state-of-the-art EmbodiedQA agents on EQAv1, exposing dataset bias.
insight: Nearly all val/test questions (all but 2 and 6) also appear in training, and answer distributions stay skewed even after entropy pruning, so memorising per-question answer priors is enough. The Majority baseline gets only 17.15%, while NN-AnswerDist gets 48.45%, showing the bias is question-specific and not just class modes. Oracle-navigation VQA (55.9/56.5) beats text-only, but the same VQA inside PACMAN's navigation falls below text-only, so the agents fail to exploit visual context.
method: Average BoW embedding: GloVe-100 word embeddings (fine-tuned) are averaged into a question vector and fed to a softmax linear classifier (fastText-like), trained with NLL using Adam, lr 5e-3, batch 64, 200 epochs, best validation-loss checkpoint.
NN-AnswerDist: for a test question, find the identical or nearest (by shared words) training question and output its most frequent training answer.
Majority baseline: always predict the most common answer.
PACMAN Q-only (LSTM): the question LSTM from the PACMAN codebase used alone, as a reproduced question-only reference.

Oracle VQA: VQA model trained on the last 5 frames of oracle navigation (50 epochs, Adam, lr 3e-4, batch 20), with the original LSTM question encoder or a BoW-CNN variant, to test the best case for visual info.
Error analysis: BoW accuracy split by question type (preposition, location, color).

setting.backbone: Average-BoW linear classifier with GloVe-100 embeddings (trained on EQAv1 questions); NN lookup; question LSTM; oracle VQA CNN+question encoder
setting.training_data: EQAv1 training questions only (7190 of 8985 total; val 862, test 933); GloVe initialization
setting.observation: question text only (no visual input) for blindfold baselines; last 5 egocentric frames under oracle navigation for the oracle VQA models
setting.action_space: none (no navigation) for blindfold baselines; oracle navigation for the VQA oracle
setting.privileged: none for blindfold baselines; oracle shortest-path navigation frames for the oracle VQA rows

numbers.extra: No environment or navigation; top-1 answer accuracy is independent of spawn distance (T10/T20/T50/Tany identical)
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Question only, BOW: 50.34 in all columns

numbers.backbone: NN over training question answer distribution

numbers.evidence: Table 1, Oracle VQA system, BOW-CNN VQA-Only 56.5

numbers_note: Accuracy is top-1 QA accuracy, not navigation metrics. Baseline table numbers (PACMAN, NMC) are from prior work and are not listed.
results: The BoW question-only model reaches 50.34% top-1, beating PACMAN (BC+REINFORCE) at 42.26/40.76 for T20/T50 and NMC (BC+A3C) at 46.21/44.32 for T20/T50. Only NMC (BC+A3C) at T10 (53.58) is better. NN-AnswerDist (48.45) beats all but PACMAN (BC+REINFORCE) and NMC (BC+A3C) at T10. BoW accuracy by question type is 9.09 for preposition, 51.72 for location and 53.31 for color.
limitations: Only EQAv1 is evaluated, with no fix proposed for the bias beyond calling for better dataset construction.
The oracle-navigation VQA comparison is unrealistic, and the paper states the oracles may not provide the best vantage points.
Preposition questions are very hard (9.09%) because they are rare in training (2.44%) and have high answer entropy.
